scope: Revision 3 routing design and abstract Lean obligations; approval is conditional on the remaining council, clean formal gate and runtime evidence.
findings: Admission binds the exact SQL, binary, profile and policy, successful derivation and preservation, and exclusion of opaque SQL. Cache reuse binds the complete request and accepted report.

The reachable-state invariant admits Parse only after successful admission, and Bind captures its accepted statement payload in a portal; Execute resolves that portal even if the statement is replaced. The model proves acceptance for Execute in a reachable state.

Revision 2 addresses mode changes before pipelined queries, indirect nested forbidden constructs, private endpoint configuration, bounded resources and transaction portal lifecycle. These are implementation obligations, not consequences of the Lean model.
Implicit transaction controls, PostgreSQL utility clients and dump/restore all remain subject to the same parser gate. Parser coverage gaps must fail closed and remain visible as unmet gates.

Revision 3 reserves cancellation capacity under session saturation, requires per-client counter deltas, independently repairs migration constraints, and records the missing root license notice without asserting redistribution rights.
limitations: The abstract strings and report flags assume faithful byte decoding, binary identity checks, parser output interpretation and forbidden production classification; no proof connects the Python implementation to Lean or the parser derivation.
The reachability model excludes Close, Simple Query invalidation, backend errors, ReadyForQuery and resource limits; tests must cover those transitions and conservative rejection.

Correctness of startup framing, concurrent pipelining, opaque-production completeness, DSN enforcement, socket isolation, shutdown and migration recovery remains unproved and demands adversarial end-to-end tests.
The clean formal gate and other council seats must complete against the final frozen specification before production changes.
Reserved cancellation capacity, per-entry-point coverage and partially applied migration repair still require runtime verification.
